purpose: the numeric standard-factor rows of Annex II point G that a BF-BOF crude steel boundary can cite, recorded as versioned references. The seed quotes the row and its offset; it never copies a bare number into code, a boundary file or an operator.

source.instrument: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2547 of 10 December 2025 laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods, OJ L 2025/2547, 22.12.2025
source.section: Annex II, point G 'STANDARD FACTORS USED IN THE MONITORING OF DIRECT EMISSIONS AT INSTALLATION LEVEL' @183800
source.license: EUR-Lex legal-document reuse under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU
source.canonicalization: drop <script> and <style> blocks, replace tags and character entities with a space, collapse whitespace, trim; SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the result
source.re_verification: a same-session re-fetch on 2026-09-21 and again on 2026-09-22 returned HTTP 202 with an empty body (AWS WAF challenge), so the hash above is the authoring-time value carried forward, not a second reading. Gap GS-02 keeps that fact attached to this record.

rows.table: Table 1 Fuel emission factors related to NCV and net calorific values per mass of fuel
rows.why_not: the seed derives its furnace carbon dioxide by the mass balance method of ST-08 rather than from a fuel duty, and blast furnace gas is a secondary gas this model does not sell or burn at a authored port (MG-S11). The row is recorded so that a later version that models gas export can cite it instead of inventing a factor.

rows.table: Table 3 Stoichiometric emission factor for process emissions from carbonate decomposition (Method A)
rows.where: the two carbonate exchanges ore-sintering::co2-sinter-carbonate-out and basic-oxygen-converter::co2-converter-flux-out, through parameters/carbon-content.json#published_constants/stoichiometric_CaCO3
rows.decimal_comma_note: 0,440 is stored as the string above and normalised to 0.440 in the carbon book, never by dropping the comma silently

rows.table: Table 3 Stoichiometric emission factor for process emissions from carbonate decomposition (Method A)
rows.why_not: no iron carbonate is authored in the burden of this model; the row matters for a siderylite or sinter-with-siderite activity, which is a different installation

rows.table: Table 5 Emission factors for process emissions from other process materials (production of iron or steel, and processing of ferrous metals)
rows.why_not: this is the activity-data side row for scrap as a process material. In this model scrap enters the carbon book through its declared carbon fraction and the ST-08 mass balance, so applying the Table 5 row on top of the mass balance would count the same carbon twice. ST-19 records the second half of the reading: the same table also carries the pig iron row, which is why these rows are factor rows for a monitoring method and not embedded emissions of the good.

rows.table: Table 5 Emission factors for process emissions from other process materials (production of iron or steel, and processing of ferrous metals)

adjacent_quote.text: Iron / iron scrap 0,0409 0,15 Steel / steel scrap 0,0109 0,04

rows.why_not: the hot metal of this model never leaves the installation and is not an input obtained from another process boundary, so no factor is applied to it (ST-15 first branch)

ST-02 gives the crude steel segment of the Annex I table the greenhouse gas column 'Carbon dioxide' only, so there is no non-CO2 gas to characterise in this boundary. The row is recorded because a seed for a different iron and steel good may need it, and because 'the table exists' is a fact the seed should not have to re-derive.

default_values_not_available.what_was_sought: the numeric default values an operator uses when actual data is incomplete, which both cached texts point at without printing

quotes.text: the applicable default values made available in accordance with Annex IV of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall be used.
ANNEX V Region-specific adaptations of default values
calculated in accordance with the methods set out in Annex IV and further specified in the implementing acts adopted pursuant to Article 7(7)

default_values_not_available.measurement: a decimal-times-tonne-CO2 pattern search over the cached S1 canonical text returns zero hits; the 28 decimal strings that do occur are all Official Journal citations in the closing notices, the first being 'OJ C 152, 6.4.2022, p. 181' at @s1:136534
default_values_not_available.blocking_fetch: the implementing act that carries the numeric table was not retrieved: EUR-Lex returned HTTP 202 with an empty body on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 and publications.europa.eu timed out from this machine. Which instrument it is has not been verified either, so this record does not name one.
default_values_not_available.consequence: every candidate item that would be reported through embedded default values stays pending (MG-S05) and is never written as zero. The boundary, precursor and mass-balance criteria of this seed are unaffected, because all of them sit in the cached and hashed text.
default_values_not_available.forbidden: inventing a default number to make a candidate item computable

runtime_consumption.note: the only row this seed derives numbers from is the Table 3 carbonate row, and it does so at authoring time through parameters/carbon-content.json. No runtime path reads this file.
